items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Joe Glazer had an assistant there, Joe Glazer was still his manager... So I just never fooled with trying to get Louie to talk about trumpet. But, uh, actually there is enough writings... You'd have to go through Joe Glazer, which would be $2,500 or something like that, too.

ctx.x: Let me move this mic a little closer to you. Your voice is soft.

Was Louis Armstrong in New York at this time playing with... Well he was traveling all around. I actually interviewed him for the book up at the, I think it was up above the Apollo Theater or someplace in that block where they were having a rehearsal. I see. And then poor Louis wanted to play the Cavalieria Rusticana. What do they call it?

intermezzo comes between acts or something there in the opera just a slow number in 3-4 time it isn't a waltz or anything just a slower thing than that and he had a very nice arrangement that he was doing and playing the melody more or less straight and Joe Glazer had an assistant there, Joe Glazer was still his manager, was already his manager had been for years I guess even then so finally his manager told him he couldn't use that number gee Louie was so mad he said someday I'm going up there and tell those so…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: Louis did make the remark, well, the only reason I play those is because Joe, meaning Joe Glazer, gets them for me free.

ctx.x: Well, you could tell me how American music got started. It started at the beginning.

So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…
